task: Retain checked types on every expression node without changing shadow parser cross-check behavior.
observation: The recursive fact walk initially treated generic constructor type syntax (for example Map[String, Int]) as expression children. Shadow mode then asserted because the simple-call projection correctly saw a type constructor where the legacy text parser saw no call. Restricting the walk to Constructor.arguments removed the assertion and kept type syntax out of expression facts.
impact: A generic AST child traversal was too broad for semantic expression facts; distinguishing expression operands from type syntax is necessary to keep checked-type coverage sound and shadow mode usable.

resolution.summary: Constructor type and type-argument nodes are excluded from expression-child traversal; default and shadow EST focused checks pass.
